newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Russia, Ukraine sign post-Soviet friendship pact.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Ukraine sign post-Soviet friendship pact.

text.p: The presidents of Ukraine and Russia on Saturday signed a long-delayed friendship treaty declaring a "strategic partnership" between the two Slav states and shaping their long-term relations in the post-Soviet period.
Ukraine's Leonid Kuchma and Russia's Boris Yeltsin signed the deal at a ceremony in Kuchma's Maryinsky palace residence in the Ukrainian capital.

The two presidents signed a further three documents including a broad political declaration outlining their views on key bilateral and international problems, statements on the disputed Black Sea Fleet and cooperation in space.

Both leaders have said the summit meeting, postponed at least six times, had become possible after lengthy talks between Kuchma and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Wednesday when they agreed terms for Moscow to keep its share of the fleet at Ukraine's Sevastopol port.

Yeltsin has signed five deals with Ukraine regarding the fleet since Kiev won independence in 1991 and Sevastopol officially became part of its territory but none of the agreements solved the problem in the long term.

Moscow and Kiev have said they are keen to end their squabbles over the Soviet heritage and dramatically improve long-term relations between the two Slav pillars of the Commonwealth of Independent States.
